findings.visibleTextExcerpt: The screenshots show the same one-column stack of large rounded cards, icon circles, pill chips, review/status panels, and a single bottom action repeated across Garden Club, Book Club, Soccer, HOA, Masjid Nur, Chess, Camera, Platform Social, Ad-Free, and Export/Migration surfaces. Book Club row b25-v4-row-010 uses the same large card, pill checklist, review box, and submit button for a nomination. Chess Club row b25-v4-row-100 uses the same shell for a club home and match result. Ad-Free row b25-v4-row-124 uses the same review/status card pattern for checkout instead of a payment checkout surface.

findings.visibleTextExcerpt: Many screenshots use copy such as "Review the details", "Final review", "Wizard progress", "Checkout review", "Local package details", and "Preview the community experience for each member role". This text describes the validation model or internal review state rather than what a real member, owner, donor, guardian, or admin would naturally see. Evidence examples: Book nomination row b25-v4-row-010 says "Review the details, editable fields, final status, and next step before saving." Masjid announcement receiver row b25-v4-row-193 still says "Review the message body, selected audience, sender, delivery timing, and member inbox state before publishing." Data Portability row b25-v4-row-130 labels the flow "Wizard progress". Persona picker row b25-v4-row-186 says "Preview the community experience for each member role." Several rows expose "Local package details" at the bottom of the app shell.
findings.requiredFix: Rewrite user-facing copy as domain product language. Remove review/spec/test phrasing and local package or persona-preview copy from production-facing screens. Put implementation metadata behind diagnostics, not in the primary community experience.

findings.visibleTextExcerpt: The screenshots are readable but not yet shippable as a modern production app. Long community names truncate in the app bar, many screens are dominated by one hue per community, and large dense cards push critical content below the fold. The repeated card layout makes unrelated tasks feel like the same screen with swapped text. Evidence examples: App bars visibly truncate long names such as Neighborhood Book Club, Riverside Youth Soccer, Cedar Commons HOA, and Data Portability Community. Most communities use a single dominant color family across background, cards, chips, and buttons. Rows such as b25-v4-row-001, b25-v4-row-010, b25-v4-row-100, b25-v4-row-124, and b25-v4-row-130 show critical content only as stacked text cards, with lower content clipped below the viewport.
findings.requiredFix: Improve production visual hierarchy: shorter responsive app-bar titles or branded headers, more varied domain components, less oversized card stacking, clearer section density, and layouts that make primary decisions visible without excessive scroll.
